questions.answer: Every electromagnetic wave travels at $3.00\times10^8$ m s$^{-1}$ in free space. Wavelength decreases as frequency increases.
questions.unit_policy: Speed unit required if a numerical speed is given.

marking_points.text: States the free-space speed as $3.00\times10^8$ m s$^{-1}$ or c.
States that wavelength decreases when frequency increases.

option_feedback.A: This is increasing wavelength, not decreasing wavelength.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Infrared has longer wavelength than visible light, which has longer wavelength than ultraviolet.
option_feedback.C: The jump from ultraviolet to microwaves increases wavelength.
option_feedback.D: Infrared has longer wavelength than visible, while ultraviolet has shorter wavelength.

option_feedback.B: Correct. 500 nm lies between 400 nm and 700 nm.
option_feedback.C: 5.0 mm is in the microwave region.
option_feedback.D: 50 m is in the radio region.

option_feedback.B: Ultraviolet is approximately $10^{-8}$ m to $4\times10^{-7}$ m.
option_feedback.C: Correct. $2.0\times10^{-10}$ m lies in the approximate X-ray range.

marking_points.text: Places visible light after infrared and before ultraviolet.

parts.answer: Approximately 400 to 700 nm, equivalent to $4.00\times10^{-7}$ m to $7.00\times10^{-7}$ m.

parts.answer: $2.3\times10^{-2}$ m is microwave; $3.0\times10^{-6}$ m is infrared; $5.5\times10^{-7}$ m is visible light.

parts.answer: Lowest to highest frequency: $2.3\times10^{-2}$ m, $3.0\times10^{-6}$ m, $5.5\times10^{-7}$ m. In free space c is constant, so frequency increases as wavelength decreases.
accepted_alternatives: microwave, infrared, visible with inverse wavelength reasoning

parts.answer: Doubling frequency halves wavelength to $4.00\times10^{-7}$ m, or 400 nm. This is at the approximate short-wavelength boundary of visible light, adjacent to ultraviolet.
accepted_alternatives: 400 nm, classified as visible at the approximate stated boundary; accept ultraviolet only with explicit acknowledgement of the approximate boundary convention.
